name: Amnon
overview: Amnon was a male member of the tribe of Judah and the firstborn son of King David. His position as the eldest son placed him in a significant role within David's family. There are no additional notes provided about him beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Amnon, which means 'trustworthy,' is a proper name mentioned in Scripture. It was not given by God but is recorded in 2 Samuel 3:2. The meaning of his name does not reflect his actions recorded later in the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Amnon was the son of King David and his wife Ahinoam. He was also the half-brother of Tamar, whom he tragically violated. These relationships are explicitly noted in Scripture and define his familial context.
scriptureSignificance: Amnon's significance lies in his role as David's firstborn and heir apparent, whose grievous sin against his half-sister Tamar led to severe family consequences. His actions brought turmoil and judgment upon David's household, highlighting the destructive power of unchecked sin. The subsequent revenge taken by Tamar's brother Absalom, resulting in Amnon's death, underscores the tragic fallout within the royal family and the broader narrative of David's troubled reign.
